subject: California killifish
title: A Parasite Makes This Fish Show Off at the Surface Until a Bird Eats It

scenes.text: Something inside this fish wants it to get eaten.
The California killifish, in the salt marshes of Southern California. Infected ones dart to the surface, jerk, and roll to flash their silver sides.
Inside the skull: hundreds of flatworm larvae, carpeting the brain. The fish eats and breeds normally. It just can't stop performing.
Ecologist Kevin Lafferty found infected fish were 10 to 30 times more likely to be eaten by a heron or egret.
That's the point. The worm can only grow up inside a bird's gut, so it changes serotonin and dopamine in the fish's brain to get there.
Its eggs leave in the bird's droppings, go into snails, then into the next fish. A parasite that steers its host into a beak.

description:
A tiny flatworm, Euhaplorchis californiensis, carpets the brain of the California killifish and makes it surface, jerk and flash its sides until a bird eats it.
The parasite's larvae enter through the gills, travel along a nerve and encyst in hundreds over the fish's brain. Infected fish behave conspicuously about four times as often as uninfected fish and, in experiments by ecologist Kevin Lafferty and colleagues, were 10 to 30 times more likely to be taken by herons and egrets. Studies of infected fish brains found altered serotonin and dopamine levels. The worm matures only in a bird's gut; eggs pass out in droppings, infect horn snails, and the cycle starts again.
Which is creepier: this, or the zombie-ant fungus?
first_comment: Hundreds of worms on one fish brain, and the fish still feeds and breeds normally. What other mind-control parasite should we cover?
